text.p: Planned maintenance on the main crude pipeline at the Russian oil export terminal at Novorossiisk on the Black Sea, originally due in February, has been postponed to early March, trading and shipping sources said.

The pipeline, which has a capacity of 90,000 tonnes per day (from a 110,000 tonne/day total) was originally due to shut for maintenance on February 20th. This was then put back to February 25th and has now been postponed until the first week of March, a shipping source said.
"But we have not had any official notice yet - we would not expect to get that until next Monday," the source added.
The maintenance was expected to take between three and four days to complete. Product exports should not be affected.
Recent closure of the port due to bad weather has caused loading delays which were going to be cleared before the maintenance began, one regular lifter said.
The port was open on Tuesday after being closed most of Monday due to high winds.
